youtube.title: Add and Subtract within 20! Number Line Rocket for Kids | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
3, 2, 1... blast off! Robo, Frog and Bunny build a number line all the way to the Moon. Add by jumping up, take away by jumping down, use the make-ten booster, find a missing number and solve space story problems within 20.
For first graders: count on, count back, make ten and fact families. Hop along on your own floor number line!

do.text: Mission Control here! Countdown to launch!
Oh! A rocket needs a number line to fly.
Let's build one, all the way to the Moon!
Twenty blocks up to the Moon!
Fun fact: twelve people have walked on the Moon.
Here's the rule. Up means add!
Take away is also called minus. They mean the same.
Start at 12. Don't count the start! Now four jumps.
Wheee! I want one more jump!
Splash! I landed in the space puddle!
Oops! One jump too far. That's 17.
Fun fact: on the Moon, you could jump much higher!
Seven jumps up. Count with Frog!
Count on, blast off! Up, up, up we go!
Here's a trick: make ten. Ten is our resting stop.
Now a missing number. 9 plus what makes 15?
Start at 9 and count the jumps to 15.
Six jumps! 9 plus 6 is 15. The missing number is 6.
First jump back 5, down to ten.
We rest at ten. Then back 1 more.
Touch down! Count back, jump back, touch down!
Same three numbers, four facts. A fact family!
Space story! 11 stars twinkle in the sky.
A cloud floats by. 4 stars hide behind it.
11 take away 4. Let's jump back on the line.
7 stars still twinkle! 11 take away 4 is 7.
Story two. 6 rockets wait on the launch pad.
How many rockets are there now?
6 plus 7. Start at 6, then make ten!
Mission quiz! Think, then shout your answer.
Seven jumps! The missing number is 7.
Time to fly home. Back down the line!
A splashdown! My kind of landing!
Fun fact: the Apollo astronauts splashed down in the ocean.
Up to add, down to take away, stop at ten!
Count on, blast off! Count back, touch down!
